definitions.explanation: Salt-cured eggs (roe) of sturgeon, served as a luxury delicacy. Widely known in Japan as one of the 'three great delicacies of the world' along with foie gras and truffles.

examples.japanese: キャビア⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{高級食材|こうきゅうしょくざい}だ。
クラッカー⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧キャビア⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{乗|の}せて→乗せる：01972_noseru⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I ate caviar on a cracker with just a little on top.

examples.japanese: キャビア⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧フォアグラ、トリュフ⟦とともに→とともに：30485_totomoni⟧⟦{世界|せかい}→世界：01447_sekai⟧⟦{三大|さんだい}→三大：29376_sandai⟧⟦{珍味|ちんみ}→珍味：05752_chinmi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Caviar, together with foie gras and truffles, is considered one of the world's three great delicacies.

notes:
Caviar specifically refers to sturgeon roe in the strict culinary sense, though the word is occasionally used loosely for fish roe of other species in casual Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- キャビア⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧: to eat caviar
- キャビア⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧: caviar dishes
- ⟦{本物|ほんもの}→本物：03628_honmono⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧キャビア: real caviar
- キャビア⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{添|そ}える→添える：13315_soeru⟧: to garnish with caviar

SIMILAR WORDS:
- いくら: salmon roe — a common, affordable Japanese roe that is sometimes compared to caviar
- ⟦{数|かず}の{子|こ}→数の子：30539_kazunoko⟧: herring roe — a traditional Japanese New Year food
- ⟦とびこ→とびこ：30538_tobiko⟧: flying fish roe — a small, crunchy roe used in sushi
- ⟦{魚卵|ぎょらん}→魚卵：15386_gyoran⟧: fish roe (general term) — the broader category that includes キャビア, いくら, and others

CULTURAL NOTE:
Caviar is strongly associated in Japan with luxury, high-end French and Russian cuisine, and special occasions. It is often mentioned in the phrase ⟦{世界|せかい}→世界：01447_sekai⟧⟦{三大|さんだい}→三大：29376_sandai⟧⟦{珍味|ちんみ}→珍味：05752_chinmi⟧ ('the world's three great delicacies'), alongside foie gras (フォアグラ) and truffles (トリュフ).
